1.why: All 12 screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary buttons are solid blue (often orange-ringed when focused) and the active step is strongly highlighted in the progress bar.

3.why: Numbered step titles, a persistent progress bar, clearly labeled fields, and a always-visible Need help? control make targets easy to locate.

4.why: The progress bar and after-action banners tell the user the next step, though she must still handle several distinct tokens/codes.

5.why: No remember-me checkbox, password-manager affordance, or autofill prompt appears on any screen.

6.why: Email is pre-filled on later steps and mock recovery values are restored into fields with explicit confirmation text.

7.why: Copy is consistently brief and plain (e.g., “one calm step at a time”, short green feedback sentences).

8.why: Only success banners are shown; no error messages appear in the screenshots, so their quality cannot be verified.

9.why: Password rules are stated and mock values are pre-filled, but everyday format examples (e.g., sample email) are largely absent.

10.why: Password and code fields are clearly labeled, yet no alternative methods (face login, etc.) are offered as choices.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one primary action and at most two related fields, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Every confirmation produces a green banner that states exactly what succeeded and what to do next.

13.why: A persistent Need help? button plus inline tips (pause reminder, password rules, next-step text) are present on every step.

14.why: Fields remain editable before confirmation and the linear flow lets the user re-enter values, though no explicit back/retry control is shown.

15.why: Header, progress bar, card layout, button styles, feedback banners, and logs are identical across all 12 steps.
